baseline:
B
A standard transformer block is primarily composed of a multi-head attention mechanism followed by a position-wise feedforward network (which is a type of MLP).

B
An MLP is defined by having at least one hidden layer between the input and output layers. The use of non-linear activation functions within these layers is what allows the network to learn complex, non-linear patterns.

B
MLPs, also known as position-wise feed-forward networks, take the context-aware outputs from the attention layer and apply further non-linear transformations to each position's embedding, allowing the model to process the information more deeply.

C
The MLP's weights are trained to recognize specific input patterns (keys) and map them to specific outputs (values), effectively creating a key-value memory system that stores factual knowledge learned from the training data.

C
The weights (W) and biases (b) are the parameters of the model that are adjusted during the training process. This tuning is how the network learns and encodes patterns from the data, effectively storing the "facts" it learns.
